brief:
- the last paragraph under "The Parent You Inherited", right after the paragraph that ends "of course your little one doesn't answer."
- what it says: the new grown-up doesn't have to win your little one over first, or win the argument inside you where the parent you inherited calls it fake, before it can start helping. It doesn't have to start as a voice in your head at all: it can be a person who likes you the way you are, a plan you wrote down on a calmer day, or one small thing you actually do to protect your little one. Those can earn trust by showing up again and again, without you having to fake a feeling.

guide_passage: Borrowed adulthood helps because the new voice does not have to win an internal election on the first day. It can arrive as an outside relationship, written plan, or concrete protective act and earn credibility through repetition.
next: The cynical voice, numbness, urge to scroll, anger, dissociation, or sudden need to do something else all belong inside the pl/ork. The response may be a protector, the child speaking directly, an inherited critic, a present-day grievance, or a blend. Start with what it is trying to prevent, accomplish, or communicate before deciding who is speaking.
